title: Message boundaries in TCP
summary: Frame length, byte buffering and sequential message extraction.
description:
# Message boundaries

TCP carries a byte stream. One socket read may contain a fragment, one complete message or several messages.

## Extracting a frame

In the studied implementation, the first two bytes contain a little-endian length. The value includes the length header itself.

```text
[ length: 2 bytes ][ message body: length - 2 bytes ]
```

1. Buffer the length header.
2. Read the message length.
3. Wait for the complete frame.
4. Pass the body to the next processing stage.
5. Continue with the remaining bytes.

Byte order applies to an individual value, not to reversing an entire message.
